Hi Amanda, it is Clara. Two changes to the alignment meeting on Wednesday. First, it moves from four o'clock to two, because the commercial director is flying out that evening. Second, the agenda is shorter. We have cut the pricing review, so there are three items only: the delayed shipment, the new supply contract, and the training on the compliance policy. You own item three, and you have ten minutes for it. One more thing, and this is the part people forget. Nobody has been taking minutes since March, so last month we repeated two decisions that were already made. I am asking each owner to write down the action items for their own item and send them to me the same day. Thank you, Amanda.

Amanda, it is Paul. I am recording this before Wednesday so that we do not spend the meeting catching up. Here is where we are. We have been negotiating with the new buyer for three weeks, and we are close, but they have been asking for a shorter payment term every single round. On the delayed shipment, the vessel has been waiting at the port since Friday and the cost is growing every day. My team has been calling the agent twice a day and getting nothing. What I need from you on Wednesday is not a legal opinion, it is a decision: do we send the formal notice now, or do we wait one more week? Bring both options and tell me what the risk is on each. See you Wednesday.

Open your item and say where things stand. Then give the one fact that everybody needs. Then raise the concern, with the reason behind it. Then propose what you want the meeting to decide. And finally, close with the action items: who does what, by when.
